items.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022
items.q: it literally was a toy piano the size of like the Linus thing

ctx.x: These circumstances from last night I got to hear a number of your original compositions and you seem to be affected by certain occurrences and then able to express your reaction to them in music, which you mentioned this incident about twenty years ago in Paris. When you sit — and you said there was a little piano after this subway incident. And I don’t know if you can describe how that emotion — probably shock — translates into a composition?

Well again I feel it’s just the music is there and you know whether it’s like I’m just capturing it and not getting in the way of it, which is kind of what happened in that situation where this song I wrote, the song “Saint Michel” which is based on that you know, 70 or so people being killed. And had it not been a beautiful day, if it had been raining I would have been on that train because it was so nice I’m going to walk. It’s going to take me an hour but I’m going to be outside, Paris the greatest city for…

but I wrote that song because it just was like, it just came out, I didn’t think actually, it really just came out. And that’s happened a number of times in my life where it’s just like I feel these things happen. In fact my mother died really tragically very quickly, and she used to talk about guardian angels. And so I wrote a song called “Guardian Angels” that came out on one of my records and then so she used to talk about this that my brother who died was like watching over me. So then I remember I did a lot…
